crop.exact_proposed_value: Yi lam: %1$d × %2$d px\ntho yung to %3$d chông thù siong. Chhài-chhiet yit chông piong hó ke thù-siong ke sṳ̀-chiet, yung tap-chhè fông-sṳt chiap to ke chông thù-siong ke nang-ngoi thù-siong khó-nèn voi sái.
crop.recommendation: Positive source-assisted semantic alignment; preserve the PFS whole-value orthographic/style gate rather than certifying inherited prefix by omission.
rationale: Read the entire prefix and warning, including Yi lam / tho yung to / chông thù siong. Its word sequence expresses the same dimensions and selected apply count as the Han prefix.

The new clause independently maps to cropping one placed parent, other images attached to that parent by snapping, and possible movement. nang-ngoi is an attested Sixian expression for other/additional, so it is semantically compatible with Han 其他 rather than a requirement for character-by-character transliteration.

The official CNS character record lists Sixian 覽 as lam55; therefore I do not flag plain lam as a missing-accent error on the basis of Mandarin/Taiwanese readings. MOE 預定 gives Sixian i55 for 預; that is phonological support, not a direct complete PFS UI spelling authority.

Unhyphenated thù siong in the prefix versus thù-siong in the warning, and lower-case tho after the Android newline versus capitalized Chhài after a full stop, make the complete value stylistically mixed. These are consistency questions, not demonstrated semantic defects or a proven mandatory PFS rule violation.

MOE ko31 nen11 and sai31 plus a directly published PFS occurrence of khó-nèn support the modal/movement analysis. I have not independently certified every PFS syllable or a compulsory segmentation policy; no acceptance is inherited from Help.
crop.unresolved: A competent Sixian PFS reviewer should settle the complete-value spelling, segmentation and capitalization policy, including the inherited prefix. Available sources do not justify calling it wrong, nor full orthographic certification.

crop.recommendation: Positive source-assisted meaning and antecedent review; qualify naturalness of the complete Shanghai-based technical wording.
rationale: The dimension prefix and 用到 %3$d 张图片 identify the selected application count. The warning conditional separately introduces a generic placed parent.

搿张图片 refers naturally to the just-mentioned cropped parent; the final 图片 heads the relative clause 接牢搿张图片个图片 and is the entity that may move. This is intelligible, though repeating 图片 and nesting 个 requires more reading effort than ideal.
有可能会移位 is explicitly non-guaranteed. No selected-versus-placed confusion or definite-readjustment wording remains.
已摆好 mixes concise formal 已 with vernacular 摆好/个/辰光. It is understandable technical prose, but less conversational than simply 摆好 or 已经摆好. I do not treat register mixing alone as a mistranslation.

Primary Shanghai-language writing supports 个, 搿, 辰光 and 有可能 constructions, not this exact technical attachment relative clause. It does not certify a pan-Wu written standard or the full warning as native idiomatic.
